articles.title: Taleb Calls H-1B Debate a 'Zero-Sum Fallacy': Foreign Workers Create Jobs
articles.excerpt: The Black Swan author says America's edge rests on other countries' brain drain — and asks whether anti-Indian racism is driving the visa backlash, days after the PERM freeze hit eight major employers.

articles.nri_angle: The case tests the limits of the OCI card for diaspora families whose children live and train in India: residence rights do not include access to BCCI domestic cricket.

articles.title: Second Judge Blocks $100,000 H-1B Fee, Including Its One-Year Extension

articles.image_caption: US District Judge Haywood Gilliam in Oakland, who ruled that agencies may not enforce the $100,000 H-1B fee without notice-and-comment rulemaking.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals, who receive the large majority of H-1B approvals, are the group most affected by whether the $100,000 fee survives in court.

articles.title: Indian National Arrested by ICE Over False Citizenship Claim to Vote in 2024 Election
articles.excerpt: Mukeshkumar Somabhai Chaudhari is charged in Minnesota with false information in voting and making a false claim of US citizenship, each carrying up to five years. DHS announced the HSI arrest on Friday; an indictment is an allegation, and he is presumed innocent.
articles.nri_angle: A clear, consequential reminder for non-citizen residents: signing a voter certificate that affirms citizenship, even once, is a federal crime separate from immigration status consequences.

articles.title: 'Never Alter or Backdate': The H-1B Document Warning From an Immigration Lawyer
articles.excerpt: Consulates are asking some long-pending H-1B applicants in India for fresh employment verification letters and social media details. A lawyer's guidance: answer truthfully, keep the email trail, and never submit a letter that claims a job exists when it does not.
articles.nri_angle: Direct, actionable guidance for Indian H-1B applicants stuck in administrative processing whose employers, jobs or circumstances may have changed since filing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.step: Get the letter from an authorized person
steps.detail: It should come from an HR representative or company official, be recently dated, and accurately confirm the job is genuine and still available.

steps.step: If the job is gone, say so — truthfully
steps.detail: Take legal advice before responding, but never submit a letter falsely claiming the job remains available.
If the letter arrives as an email attachment, retain the original email and include a printout with the letter where appropriate.

steps.step: Send social media details through the designated channel
steps.detail: Social media disclosure has been mandatory for H-1B applicants since last December; make sure links are accurate and accessible.
Do not edit dates, signatures or letterheads, and do not obtain verification from an unauthorized person.

articles.title: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia Is Out After Five Days and One Briefing

articles.title: House Bill Would Lift H-1B Salary Exemption Threshold Toward $140,000
articles.excerpt: Rep. Glenn Grothman's bill, matching Sen. Jon Husted's Senate version, would replace the $60,000 threshold frozen since 1998 with twice the National Average Wage Index — nearly $140,000 today — for H-1B-dependent employers using the salary exemption.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals are the largest H-1B group, and those at H-1B-dependent firms paid between $60,000 and $140,000 would lose the salary-exemption shortcut if this bill passes.

articles.title: Four Manchester Universities Offer £10,000 GREAT Scholarships to Indian Students

articles.image_caption: Whitworth Hall at the University of Manchester. Four Manchester universities are offering £10,000 GREAT Scholarships to Indian students.

articles.title: Arizona DACA Renewals Now Take Five to Six Months as Delays Cost Jobs and Licences
articles.excerpt: Arizona advocates say renewal waits have stretched from about two months to five or six months under new USCIS screening and biometrics requirements. CBS News reports the national backlog of pending renewals has passed 125,000.
articles.image_caption: A USCIS I-797 Notice of Action for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA). Arizona DACA renewals now take five to six months, costing recipients jobs and licences.
articles.nri_angle: Arizona is home to 16,000-20,000 DACA recipients; when a renewal lapses, work authorization and driver licences lapse with it, and advocates say calls for help now arrive daily.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DHS Makes End of 540-Day Work Permit Extension Permanent in Final Rule
articles.excerpt: The Department of Homeland Security's final rule, effective on Federal Register publication on October 14, means most EAD renewals filed on or after October 30, 2025 no longer extend work authorization while they are pending — a direct hit for H-4 spouses and asylum applicants.
articles.image_caption: The US Department of Homeland Security headquarters in Washington, DC. DHS made the end of the 540-day work permit extension permanent in a final rule.
articles.nri_angle: H-4 spouses of H-1B workers — most of them Indian women — lose the safety net that kept them employed while USCIS processed renewals; a pending renewal no longer extends the card past its printed expiry date.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DHS Proposes Ending Deference to Prior H-1B and L-1 Petition Approvals
articles.excerpt: A proposed rule would remove the requirement that USCIS defer to earlier I-129 approvals, exposing H-1B and L-1 extensions and amendments to fresh adjudication, more evidence requests, and higher denial risk.
articles.image_caption: The US Department of Homeland Security headquarters in Washington, DC. DHS has proposed ending automatic deference to prior H-1B and L-1 petition approvals.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals are a large share of H-1B holders and file repeated extensions while awaiting green cards, so losing deference to prior approvals would make renewals less predictable for workers and employers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iowa City Mother of Four Deported to Sierra Leone Before a Judge Heard Her Case
articles.excerpt: Fatou Traore, in the US for over 20 years and protected from return to Ivory Coast since 2011, was removed to a country she has never visited, advocates say.
articles.image_caption: Downtown Iowa City, Iowa, in a photograph from Wikimedia Commons. Fatou Traore lived in Iowa City for more than 20 years before she was deported on October 13.
articles.nri_angle: A third-country removal carried out despite a 2011 withholding order shows immigrant families why pending protections need active legal confirmation, not assumptions.

articles.title: Federal Agents Search Ilhan Omar's Washington Home Under Court-Authorized Warrant
articles.excerpt: The Justice Department said Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorised warrant on October 12 as part of an ongoing investigation. Omar denies wrongdoing, no charges have been reported, and she called the search an attempt to target political enemies.
articles.image_caption: Rep. Ilhan Omar, whose Washington home was searched by federal agents under a court-authorised warrant on October 12.

articles.image_caption: The Radcliffe Camera at the University of Oxford. UK universities are withdrawing offers to international students to protect their sponsor licences as visa refusals rise.
articles.nri_angle: Indian applicants are caught in a UK compliance squeeze: withdrawals of Indian study-visa applications quadrupled to 5.2%, and some universities have added extra screening for Indian applicants.

articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump, whose administration appealed the ruling that froze the $100,000 H-1B fee.

articles.title: Green Cards Reflect Cases Started Years Ago: Attorney's Five-Point Rebuttal
articles.excerpt: Gnanamookan Senthurjothi's five points: green cards issued today trace to 2013–2014 filings, PERM already protects laid-off Americans, and arithmetic is not evidence.
articles.image_caption: A US passport, green card and Statue of Liberty figurine arranged for an illustration. An immigration attorney argues recent green cards reflect cases filed years ago, not a sudden surge.
articles.nri_angle: The workers in the administration's crosshairs are largely long-tenured Indian professionals stuck in the longest green-card backlog, not recent arrivals — a framing that matters for both morale and expected court challenges.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: H-1B approvals are not new hires.
Roles are not interchangeable.
Green cards reflect long-standing applications.
Displacement safeguards are already in place.
Investigate with evidence, not just numbers.

articles.title: 'H-1B Is a Business Model': Trump Official Defends Green-Card Suspensions
articles.excerpt: Labor Department inspector general Anthony D'Esposito says tech companies use H-1B visas to replace American workers, defending the PERM freeze on Microsoft, Adobe and six IT firms.
articles.image_caption: Donald Trump speaks to reporters. A Trump administration official defended the suspension of Microsoft, Adobe and six IT firms from the green card program, calling H-1B a business model.
articles.nri_angle: Indians account for ~71% of H-1B holders and the suspended firms include the five largest Indian IT exporters, putting Indian green-card queues under the longest shadow of the freeze.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why Trump's H-1B Crackdown Could Be an 'Own Goal' for America
articles.excerpt: The Times of India argues the $100,000 fee, fraud probes and green-card freezes will push innovation offshore — an industrial-policy gift to India disguised as worker protection.
articles.image_caption: Donald Trump climbs the stairs of a presidential aircraft. The Times of India analysis argues his H-1B crackdown is an own goal that risks handing skilled workers to rival economies.
articles.nri_angle: TOI argues the crackdown hands India an advantage: offshoring acceleration and GCC growth give Indian professionals credible onshore alternatives to decade-long US green-card queues.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Fee may choke US innovation.
Offshoring predicted to surge within a year.
Domestic backlash from US lawmakers.
Indian tech sector gaining momentum.

articles.title: Trump Honors Immigrant Tech CEOs Hours After Vance Suspends Microsoft Green-Card Filings
articles.excerpt: Five of the six tech leaders who received America's top science and technology medals on Thursday are immigrants — honored the same day the administration accused Microsoft of abusing the visa system.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump presents Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the certificate for the National Medal of Technology and Innovation at the White House science summit on Oct. 8, 2026, as Nadella holds the medal in its case. The ceremony came hours after Vice President JD Vance announced that Microsoft was being suspended from the federal program that lets employers sponsor foreign workers for green cards.
articles.nri_angle: Five of six honorees are immigrants including Indian-born Satya Nadella, while the same-day crackdown freezes employer green-card sponsorship at Microsoft and major Indian IT consultancies that sponsor thousands of Indian H-1B workers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jayapal Condemns Suspension of Microsoft From Green Card Programme
articles.excerpt: The Indian-American lawmaker called the PERM crackdown a 'biased and punitive misuse of the law' that threatens legal immigration; the White House fired back.
articles.image_caption: The Microsoft logo on a company office building. The Trump administration suspended Microsoft and seven other tech firms from the PERM labour-certification programme, a move Rep. Pramila Jayapal condemned as a punitive misuse of the law.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals, who dominate employment-based green-card applications with waits past 11 years, lose a key sponsorship route at eight major employers, making PERM status and alternate routes the urgent question for thousands of H-1B families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Federal Court Postpones Rule Ending Duration of Status for Student Visas
articles.excerpt: A federal judge in Massachusetts issued a nationwide injunction one day before a DHS rule was set to replace open-ended duration-of-status admissions with four-year caps for F and J visa holders — keeping the old system alive while the government appeals.
articles.image_caption: Students on a US university campus. A federal court has postponed a rule ending duration of status for student visas.
articles.nri_angle: Roughly 352,000 Indian students — the largest international-student cohort in the U.S. — are directly affected: the blocked rule's four-year cap and discretionary extension process would have hit Indian PhD and STEM OPT students hardest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Former Envoy Warns Trump's Green Card Curbs May Rupture India-US Ties
articles.excerpt: Former Indian ambassador Javed Ashraf told NDTV that US restrictions on students, H-1B workers and green-card applicants are eroding the "social bridge" between the two countries, days after Washington froze PERM applications for eight major firms including Microsoft, Infosys and TCS.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump. A former Indian envoy warns his green-card curbs may rupture India-US ties.
articles.nri_angle: The PERM freeze directly hits the green-card pipeline that hundreds of thousands of Indian H-1B workers at Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL and Cognizant rely on — and a former Indian envoy warns the cumulative US curbs could strain the diaspora's foundational role in the India-US relationship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
